Every pair differs in count (3 or 2–3 vs 1), but every pair also differs in other stated properties: category (A vs C or D), destination (AST-013 vs ADR-MP-06 or candidate backlog), and stated non-promotion reason (scope, non-generalization, prior ruling). notes: In R-36, 'stop-at-architectural-uncertainty' is promoted, yet the matrix lists #7 as 'already' with 'No delta ... do not duplicate it'. R-36 also promotes 'implementation-evidence-outweighs-unverified-theory', which is not in the matrix at all. R-36 says '2 added by ARB at review'. This shows R-36, not the matrix, decides outcomes.

The coded 'e' conflates units. For promoted items it is a threshold bucket ('2+') derived from slice counts. For non-promoted items it is a raw '1' in slices (#5), contexts (#14), or an unstated unit (#17).
The coded fields t='AST-013' and k='engineering-behaviour' for the non-promoted items are not stated by the sources. #5 is routed to ADR-MP-06 (C); #14 and #17 go to the candidate backlog (D).
The coded ground='RULE' for all three refusals is not supported uniformly. #5 is refused on scope, #14 on non-generalization, and only #17 on a prior ruling.
Under a reading that uses only the coded fields (a, k, t, cluster), all 12 pairs would look matched. Those fields are coder-assigned and not stated by the sources, so they are not counted.
